title: [B1 • Band 5.0] Bài 311: The Architecture of Ignorance: Rethinking Scientific Progress
passageHtml:
PASSAGE 311 (LEVEL B1 • BAND 5.0)

The Architecture of Ignorance: Rethinking Scientific Progress

Paragraph 1. Standard school textbooks describe scientific progress as a steady climb toward complete truth. Each generation is shown building neatly upon past discoveries until nature's secrets are fully solved. However, in The Ignorance Ledger, science philosopher Dr. Aris Thorne challenges this tidy story. True breakthroughs, he explains, do not merely expand human knowledge; their main result is creating entirely new categories of things we realize we do not know.

Paragraph 2. Thorne separates passive ignorance from active, strategic ignorance. Passive ignorance is simply lacking basic information—the everyday state of an untrained mind. By contrast, strategic ignorance is an advanced awareness produced only by top-level science. When physicists discovered quantum mechanics in the early twentieth century, they did not tidy up classical physics; instead, they broke Newton's predictable rules and revealed vast new mysteries inside the atom. Similarly, discovering DNA did not close biology, but exposed the puzzling world of epigenetics.

Paragraph 3. A major target of Thorne's criticism is today's obsession with measuring scientists purely through numbers. University ranking committees and research councils judge scholars mostly by counting published papers, citation scores, and quick business profits. Because agencies demand safe, predictable results, bold studies that challenge old ideas are starved of institutional funding, pushing researchers toward dull, low-risk topics.

Paragraph 4. In his closing chapters, Thorne urges a deep reform in science education. Instead of rewarding scholars who claim to hold final answers, universities should celebrate those who design smarter, deeper questions. Ignorance is not an embarrassing weakness to hide, Thorne insists; it is the vital fuel that keeps real science moving forward.

groups.title: Questions 8–10
groups.instructions: Do the following statements agree with the claims of the writer? Write YES, NO, or NOT GIVEN.

q1.text: What is Dr. Thorne's main argument in Paragraph 1?
options: A. Science textbooks should be banned from universities.
B. Modern researchers produce fewer facts than earlier scholars.
C. Major scientific discoveries reveal brand-new areas of unknown questions.
D. Ordinary citizens no longer trust laboratory scientists.

steps: Đoạn 1: Đột phá thật sự tạo ra những hạng mục chưa biết hoàn toàn mới.

options: A. A simple lack of basic facts found in an untrained mind
B. A deliberate refusal to read scientific books
C. A complex state created by quantum physics
D. A temporary error caused by faulty lab tools

steps: Đoạn 2: "...simply lacking basic information—the everyday state of an untrained mind."

q3.text: Why does Thorne criticise research councils in Paragraph 3?
options: A. They publish too many difficult books for students.
B. They let politicians write university exam papers.
C. They give most of their money to young undergraduate students.
D. They judge scientists strictly by paper counts and short-term profits.

steps: Đoạn 3: Chỉ chấm điểm dựa vào số lượng bài báo, trích dẫn và lợi nhuận kinh doanh nhanh.

q4.text: What reform does Thorne recommend in the final paragraph?
options: A. Paying higher salaries to university ranking managers
B. Valuing scientists who ask deeper questions over those claiming final answers
C. Requiring all researchers to repeat Newton's experiments
D. Cutting public money for university biology labs

steps: Đoạn 4: Nên tôn vinh những người thiết kế được câu hỏi sâu sắc hơn.
Đoạn 2: "Passive ignorance is simply lacking basic information..."

q8.text: Quantum mechanics proved that Newton's classical rules explained every atomic behaviour.

steps: Đoạn 2: Cơ học lượng tử đã phá vỡ quy tắc dự đoán cũ của Newton (broke Newton's predictable rules).

q9.text: Academic institutions ought to value researchers who formulate thoughtful questions.

steps: Đoạn 4: "...universities should celebrate those who design smarter, deeper questions."

q10.text: Private technology firms fund bold science better than government councils do.

steps: Đoạn 3: Bài chỉ phê phán quỹ nghiên cứu thích lợi nhuận nhanh, không so sánh quỹ tư nhân với quỹ chính phủ.
